column1: Just as an increase in government purchases has a multiplied effect on income, so does a decrease in taxes. As before, the initial change in expenditure, now MPC 3 DT, is multiplied by 1/(1 2 MPC). The overall effect on income of the change in taxes is DY/DT  2MPC/(1 2 MPC). This expression is the tax multiplier, the amount income changes in response to a $1 change in taxes. (The negative sign indicates that income moves in the opposite direction from taxes.) For example, if the marginal propensity to consume is 0.6, then the tax multiplier is DY/DT  20.6/(1 2 0.6) 5 21.5. In this example, a $1.00 cut in taxes raises equilibrium income by $1.50.
